slides.title: How it works
slides.html: A forward observer officer (FOO) asks for drones. The HQ or a platoon's TOC gives the request to a drone team, which flies and reports to the FOO's Inbox.

slides.title: Roles
slides.html: Each role does one part of the job, from asking for a drone to flying it. A phone has one role, and Drones shows only that role's pages.

slides.title: Forward observer officer (FOO)
slides.html: The FOO asks for drones and follows each request. My requests shows where each one stands, such as Waiting for the HQ.

slides.title: HQ
slides.html: The HQ gives requests to drone teams with Assign and draws corridors, where teams may fly. Only the HQ gives quotas, a set number of requests a day.

slides.title: TOC
slides.html: A TOC, a platoon's tactical operations centre, works like the HQ for its own teams. It gives them requests with Assign and draws their corridors, but gives no quotas.

slides.title: Drone team
slides.html: The team's navigator, or crew observer, takes the Drone team role. They list the team's drones, plan each mission, run it and report how it went.

slides.title: Pilot
slides.html: The Pilot role is for the drone team's second phone. Its one page gives the bearing and distance from drone to target, the planned height and the flight time left.

slides.title: Requests
slides.html: A request asks for a Strike or a Recon on an enemy mark or area. To says who should answer, and a request no team takes lapses after two hours.

slides.title: Corridors
slides.html: A corridor is the area where a team may fly, for set hours. It shows shaded on the map, and a plan warns if its route leaves the corridor.

slides.title: Quotas
slides.html: A quota gives a FOO, or a whole unit, a set number of requests a day on one team. The Request sheet then lists that team first under To.

slides.title: Missions and plans
slides.html: A mission is one drone flight on a request, such as Strike 1. Its plan warns about Range, and Weather if turned on, but the team decides.

slides.title: Drone types
slides.html: A drone team lists its drone types with their range, flight time and count. Plans use these limits, and the HQ and TOC see which team has drones that fit.

slides.title: What everyone sees
slides.html: Phones on the drone feeds show corridors, routes, drones and the circle around each target, even without OpenDefence UAVOps. In OpenDefence UAVOps, Watch on a flying mission opens its video.

slides.title: A plugin on OpenDefence Main
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps is a separate plugin that works through OpenDefence Main's Request sheet and Inbox. If an admin turns Quotas and corridors Off, requests go straight to the teams.
